Purpose: This page introduces Bevy's Entity Component System architecture, explaining the fundamental concepts of entities, components, systems, and the World. It provides a high-level overview of how these elements work together to enable data-driven game development.

Scope: This is a parent page. For detailed technical specifications, see the following child pages:

  • World and Entity Management — Document the World as the central data store, entity lifecycle (allocation, spawning, despawning), and the EntityAllocator's generational index system. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs93-110
  • Components and Bundles — Explain component registration, bundle composition, required components, and component hooks (on_add, on_insert, on_remove). crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs32-55
  • Systems and SystemParams — Document system functions, SystemParam trait, common parameters (Query, Res, ResMut, Commands, Local), and the SystemParam lifecycle (init_state, validate_param, get_param). crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/system_param.rs41-86
  • Queries and Filters — Explain Query<D, F> system parameter, QueryData and QueryFilter traits, query iteration patterns, and query caching via QueryState. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/query.rs22-57
  • Commands and Deferred Operations — Document the Commands system for deferred structural changes, command queue mechanics, ApplyDeferred system, EntityCommands API, and the BevyError/Severity/FallbackErrorHandler error handling system for fallible systems and commands. Covers panic-to-error conversion and context chaining. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/commands/mod.rs41-57 crates/bevy_ecs/src/lib.rs77-78
  • Change Detection — Explain change detection via Added<T> and Changed<T> filters, Tick-based tracking, and Ref<T>/Mut<T> wrappers. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs16-19
  • Archetypes and Storage — Document archetype-based storage, table vs sparse-set storage, archetype transitions, and how they enable efficient query iteration. crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/state.rs34-54
  • Observers and Relationships — Document the observer pattern for reactive ECS logic, entity relationships (parent/child via bevy_hierarchy), entity disabling, and the relationship source collection system. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs45-54

Core ECS Concepts

Bevy's ECS is built on four fundamental concepts:

ConceptDescriptionPrimary Type
EntityUnique identifier for a "thing" in the game worldEntity crates/bevy_ecs/src/lib.rs76
ComponentData associated with an entityComponent crates/bevy_ecs/src/lib.rs75
SystemLogic that operates on entities with specific componentsSystem crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/mod.rs151
WorldContainer storing all entities, components, and resourcesWorld crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs93

Entities

An Entity is a lightweight identifier consisting of a u32 index and a u32 generation. It identifies a "game object" but contains no data itself. Entities follow a specific lifecycle managed by the EntityAllocator, which handles concurrent allocation of IDs. Generations are incremented when an entity is freed, ensuring that stale references to the same index are invalidated.

Sources: crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs95-101 crates/bevy_ecs/src/lib.rs76 crates/bevy_ecs/src/entity/mod.rs60-75

Components

Components are Rust types that implement the Component trait. They store data associated with entities. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs79-83 Each entity can have zero or one instance of each component type. Components are stored in either Table (dense, optimized for iteration) or SparseSet (optimized for rapid insertion/removal) storage. crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/fetch.rs8-15 Bevy also supports Required Components, which automatically spawn dependencies when a component is added. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs41-45

Sources: crates/bevy_ecs/src/lib.rs75-80 crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/fetch.rs27-62 crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs41-45

Systems

Systems are logic functions that declare their data dependencies through SystemParam parameters. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/mod.rs1-11 Bevy automatically parallelizes systems that do not have conflicting mutable access to the same data. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/mod.rs37-43 Systems can return () or a Result<T, BevyError>, allowing integration with a centralized error handling system that converts panics to errors and passes them to a FallbackErrorHandler. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/mod.rs84-85 crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/commands/mod.rs88-92

Sources: crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/mod.rs1-110 crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/system_param.rs41-85 crates/bevy_ecs/src/lib.rs77-78

World

The World is the central data store. It maintains:

  • Entities: Metadata and location of every entity via the Entities struct. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs95
  • EntityAllocator: Handles concurrent allocation of entity IDs. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs96
  • Components: Registry of component types and their metadata. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs97
  • Archetypes: Groups of entities with identical component sets. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs100
  • Storages: The actual raw data buffers for components. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs101
  • Resources: Singleton data types stored outside the entity/archetype structure. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs86-92

Sources: crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs74-110

System Parameter Types

Systems use SystemParam to request data from the World. The SystemParam trait defines a lifecycle including init_state, validate_param, and get_param. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/system_param.rs138-160

Parameter TypeAccessDescription

Query System

Queries provide selective access to entity data. They consist of QueryData (what to fetch) and QueryFilter (what to exclude). crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/query.rs22-36

  • QueryData: Includes &T, &mut T, Option<&T>, Entity, Ref<T>, Mut<T>, and tuples thereof (up to 15 elements). crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/fetch.rs27-62
  • QueryFilter: Includes With<T>, Without<T>, Added<T>, Changed<T>, Or<F>, and AnyOf. crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/fetch.rs53-61 crates/bevy_ecs/src/lib.rs86-87

Sources: crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/query.rs22-230 crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/fetch.rs27-176

Archetype-Based Storage

Bevy organizes entities into Archetypes. An archetype is a unique set of component types; all entities in the same archetype have exactly the same components. crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs100

This architecture allows QueryIter to iterate over contiguous arrays of data (Tables) for entities in the same archetype, maximizing CPU cache efficiency. crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/state.rs59-68 crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/iter.rs188-196 Archetypes enable "dense" iteration where the query skips entities that do not match the required component layout. crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/state.rs94-96

Sources: crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs93-110 crates/bevy_ecs/src/query/state.rs56-101

Commands and Deferred Mutations

Structural changes like spawning entities or adding components require exclusive access to the World. To allow these operations from parallel systems, Bevy uses Commands to queue changes in a CommandQueue. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/commands/mod.rs43-57

Queued commands are applied during synchronization points, typically by the ApplyDeferred system. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/commands/mod.rs40-41 The command system includes advanced error handling where BevyError supports context chaining via the .context() method and results are processed by the FallbackErrorHandler. crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/commands/mod.rs88-95 crates/bevy_ecs/src/lib.rs77-78

Sources: crates/bevy_ecs/src/system/commands/mod.rs41-103 crates/bevy_ecs/src/world/mod.rs109-150
